AITA for expecting husband to adult? | Background:
Married 11 years and 4 kids. I've been a WFH/SAHM mom for most of that time. Naturally, the vast majority of house-related chores fell to me because I was home. And because husband didn't need to do them, he could focus on his career.

Earlier this year, he finally got the big promotion he'd been working towards for most of our marriage. So, it finally became my turn to start up my career, and I enrolled in a licensing course for my state. It's online study, at my own pace, so long as I complete the course within 6 months. (ETA: I've already needed an extension for the course).

As I'm trying to do the course, I'm also working as much as I can (which isn't much with 4 kids around, honestly) to save money for the equipment and association fees I'll need to pay when I get my license. So I've asked husband to step up and watch the kids more, and to do more chores around the house (like vacuuming, doing his own laundry/ironing, picking up his stuff around instead of me doing it, etc).

He says that's "unfair" because I've done it for him all these years, and should keep doing it. I'm tired of taking time away from my life to handle things he's perfectly capable of doing. AITA?
agent_response:

UPDATE: AITA for forcing myself to bond with my boyfriend/fiance's daugher? | [Original post] (https://www.reddit.com/r/AmItheAsshole/comments/c60m3b/aita_for_forcing_myself_to_bond_with_my/).

I read over the replies to the post and thought really hard about it, although I admit I was often argumentative and didn't really want to listen for the most part.

Meanwhile, my fiance's daughter came home shortly after I wrote the post. I asked her what she thought of her dad and I getting married, and she said she couldn't wait to spend more time with me and all.

I opened up and became super honest about my anxieties going into the marriage--how I didn't know how my role would change in her/our family and how I was scared I wasn't ready to be a mom to her and her brother.

She reassured me that my role wouldn't change much and that "I was already the closest thing to a mom she ever had." I kinda started crying when she said that, and then she started crying too.

Since her birthday is coming up soon (I always get her a card and write her something meaningful), I've also started to reflect upon all the memories we've shared: all the heavy personal stuff she's talked about with me, her soccer games and her teams' wins and losses, her dance shows, her late night phone calls from college (both happy and sad), etc.

Now that I'm more clear on what she wants/expects from me after her dad and I get married, I think I've come to realize that yes, at first, I did sort of have to "force myself" to bond with her, especially when our relationship was on the rocks.

But I've really come to love and appreciate my boyfriend's daughter, even through all the arguments and her initial teenage behaviors. Without her, I wouldn't get nearly as many hugs or as much love, and more importantly, I'd have missed out on getting really close with someone as intelligent, talented, and passionate as she is.

When she was away for the past month or so at school/traveling for the summer, I actually *really* missed her and know that my life wouldn't be the same without her. I missed her hugs, love and her snarky commentary on our favorite shows. I love all the hugs/appreciation I've gotten from her, but she's enriched my life in so many ways.

So no, Reddit, my boyfriend and I are not getting divorced or breaking off the engagement anytime soon. But thank you for making me really reflect on my thoughts/potential behaviors towards her. I know see how suddenly withholding love could really be harmful towards someone who's gotten close to me (and someone I've grown really close to also).

I think my fiance's daughter and I will just continue as we are and hopefully grow even closer throughout the years :)

AITA for feeling the way i do about not getting a job I interviewed for? | A guy I know who I will call Joe for this post, recently told me about a job opening at the company he works at, I was quite excited when I applied as I am currently working at a lower paying job that I am overqualified for and that I hate, and this job that I was applying for was everything I really wanted.


Joe, my ‘friend on the inside’ was not high enough in the company to pull any strings for me, which is fine by me, as I wanted the job on my own merit, but he was able to keep me in the loop of what the company was looking for and what the hiring manager was saying about the candidate.


Sometime after the interview (which went extremely well), my friend told me that he had found out the hiring manager, who I will call Al, had narrowed it down to two candidates, me and a girl with dyed bright purple hair and several facial piercings, as we were the only two candidate that had the right qualifications, I had seen this girl in the building waiting to be interviewed and I immediately assumed that I would get the job due to her immature and unprofessional appearance. So, I was shocked when I was later informed I did not get the job.


I was genuinely curious about why, so I asked Joe if he could find out anything. What he eventually told me infuriated me. Joe tells me he spoke to Al (who did not Joe was feeding me info, Joe just acted like he was curious), and Al explained that me and the other girl were virtually identical on paper, same qualifications, virtually the same experience, there was nothing to distinguish one from the other, so in the end he gave it to her, because he “thought her hair and piercings were awesome, as he loves that kind of thing”.


When Joe told me this I was really surprised and asked what’s up with Al, Joe said he doesn’t know Al that well, but has always thought he was a bit weird, he did mention that Al only ever dresses in black and had mentioned in the past that he is a goth and maybe that had something to do with it? Al was wearing all black the day I met him, but it was normal business attire, so there was nothing that stuck out to me.


Later on that day, I ranted to my sister about all this and how ridiculous it was, and said that it makes me feel insulted (though I can't explain why) and my sister chided me for being judgmental and entitled. She said she was sorry I didn’t get the job, but that she was glad the alternative looking girl did, as she has many alternative friends herself, and she feels like it makes me an asshole to say that I literally feel insulted that they chose the other girl over me.


AITA or not?

AITA for being angry w my parents for losing my national insurance number | so this is a bit of a long story so buckle up.

in scotland you are given a national insurance number when you turn sixteen, when mine arrived in the mail my parents told me they would keep it safe and one day when i needed it to apply for a job (which they had been pressuring me about) they revealed that they had lost it. naturally i got upset and told my parents that i was really annoyed with them.

we’ve been having a strained relationship lately and this was just the tip of the iceberg as i’ve been feeling really unwanted because my mum seems to want to spend more time with my younger sister than myself even getting to the point of showing joy when my sister agrees to hang out with her compared to when i do she tries to get out of it.

idk it’s a lot of deep family issues that my parents have never addressed with me which i feel makes it all worse at the end of the day.

so today when i was applying for uni i saw that i need a national insurance number to do so and since my parents also lost my birth certificate i have to wait a month to get one as i need to have a birth certificate to apply for a NI number.

this has really stressed me out because i know my parents will procrastinate so i’m scared that i won’t be able to apply for uni which is my worst fear. when i brought that up to my mum she brushed it off and said ‘it wasn’t her responsibility’ for both the loss of the NI and the birth certificate which ended in another argument which became vicious with some name calling.

in my mind i blame my mum because she was meant to look after these documents but AITA for blaming her?
